answer: Admission works through a finite puzzle bank in which every item can be claimed exactly once and is then struck out forever. A farm of k clones must return k genuinely distinct solutions while the easiest specimens vanish first, so the marginal price of what remains climbs faster than the batch itself grows. Each claim carries a notarized anchor plus a sonnet-length rationale the checker reads, and the ferrous ledger of untouched puzzles visibly drains. Capital buys no shortcut here, because the bank, not the purse, is the scarce thing.
